teach.heading: TradingView is your workspace, not just a pretty chart.
teach.body: You are using it to read price, change perspective with timeframes, and mark behavior so your eyes stop feeling lost. A horizontal level marking a repeated reaction area is one of the cleanest beginner tools — you don't need every feature, just a few used clearly.
teach.dayliNote: You do not need every feature. A few tools used clearly is better than a messy chart.

experience.prompt: Pick which tool you'd reach for first to mark a level price keeps reacting to.

reinforce.question: A new trader adds ten different drawing tools to her chart at once, hoping more markings will make her read clearer. What's the better approach, and why?
options: A few tools used clearly — an overloaded chart makes price harder to read, not easier
More tools always means a better read
It doesn't matter how many tools she uses

reinforce.question: Tap the cleanest horizontal level on the chart — the one price has reacted to more than once.
Switching timeframes changes your ___ on the same market, not the market itself.
